notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch) reached the homepage and Home & Lifestyle department page and pulled the embedded SSR JSON (react-helmet/page-state), which surfaced the department's 'SEASONAL' mega-menu block (Food Gifts, Halloween Shop, Fall Decor, Fall Entertaining) and the master 'Holiday Decor' category (catId cat1002110011) that all named-holiday PLPs are built from via an 'event'/'item_type'/'product_type' facet system. Tier 1 could not read live product counts because the grid is hydrated client-side via a Constructor.io browse call (ac.cnstrc.com) with no key/results embedded in SSR HTML. Tier 2 (Playwright/Chromium via local venv) was attempted next and hit a hard connection-level block: every navigation, including the plain homepage, failed with net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR (tried default and --disable-http2 launch args, both failed; confirmed not transient by retrying homepage alone) -- consistent with Akamai/bot-detection fingerprinting headless Chromium at the TLS/HTTP2 layer. Per the hard-block rule this moved to Tier 3 (Claude-in-Chrome), which loaded every page normally with real rendered product counts. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (checked before Tier 3 use). Discovery: verified 6 event/theme facet values by finding them as real hrefs in the site's own rendered DOM (mega-menu + in-page subcategory tiles), not by guessing: event=christmas, event=halloween, event=thanksgiving, event=valentines, event=easter, theme=americana. A 7th guess (event=new+year) rendered a plausible-looking SEO title ('New Year Holiday Decor') but was NOT found linked anywhere in real navigation -- this looks like a URL-template artifact rather than a genuine site-presented category, so it was excluded per the no-fabrication rule; it also returned 0 results. Checked internal search for 'diwali' -- zero results, no Diwali/Holi/Eid presence anywhere in nav or mega-menu, consistent with a US-only department store; no dedicated New Year PLP found through real navigation either. The homepage/global 'Halloween Shop' banner link (id=cat1009090003) is a separate sitewide (all-department: costumes/candy/apparel) hub, not Home-department decor, and was excluded as out of scope per the Home-department-only instruction; the Home-department-scoped Halloween node (event=halloween under cat1002110011, reached via the Home & Lifestyle SEASONAL menu) was used instead. Within 'Christmas Decorations' (event=christmas, id=cat1002110011, 5192 results total -- this total is a superset of its own child facets below, so per the parent/child rule it is recorded as a grouping row, qty null, to avoid double counting), the page's own subcategory tiles were evaluated individually: 9 of them are genuine item_type/product_type facet PLPs of the same category (kept as Christmas sub-rows with their own exact counts) and one ('Porch & Outdoor') resolves to a separate genuine category (Outdoor Christmas Decor, cat100260272) so it was kept as its own row. Two tiles were excluded after inspection: 'Candles' links to the general (non-Christmas-specific) Candles & Home Fragrance category (cat100240140) -- excluded per the seasonal-product-in-normal-category rule; 'Gingerbread' links to an internal keyword search page (/s?searchTerm=gingerbread) -- excluded as a search-result page, not a PLP. Halloween, Thanksgiving, Valentine's Day, Easter and Independence Day (Americana/4th of July) were each captured as single rows at their own event-level PLP (own URL, own title, own exact count) without further decomposing their sub-tiles, since each page is itself already a genuine self-contained category listing and the accuracy/coverage tradeoff favored verifying the primary node precisely for every holiday over exhaustively drilling every holiday to the same depth as Christmas. 'Thanksgiving' actually renders as one combined node titled 'Thanksgiving & Fall Decor' (rendered site title, not a Thanksgiving-only listing) -- recorded faithfully under category Thanksgiving with that literal sub_category name. 'Outdoor Christmas Decor' and 'Valentines Holiday Decor' are real, distinct category pages (own title, own description, own breadcrumb, own sub-tiles) that currently return 'Your filters produced 0 results' -- kept as rows with qty 0 and a MANUAL REVIEW flag (checked 2026-09-04, early September) rather than treated as absent, since the taxonomy node itself is genuine and this looks like seasonal restocking timing rather than a nonexistent category. No duplicate-URL rows were kept (checked all links for exact duplicates -- none).
